content.text:
Base directory for this skill: D:\Apps\micro1-frontier-hackathon\runtime\.claude\skills\aliasbreaker

Run one AliasBreaker campaign following the protocol in CLAUDE.md exactly.

- CASE = the fixture path given in the arguments (e.g.
  `../data/cases/dev/case-101.json`).
- RUN = `runs/<run-id>` if a run id was given, else `runs/<case-id>-manual`.

Begin with `start`, follow the decision guidance, and end with `finalize`.
All hard rules in CLAUDE.md apply unchanged.


ARGUMENTS: ../data/cases/dev/case-103.json runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 1 --why "Broad discriminator at t=35.32 separates many lower-support candidate pairs at once, testing whether candidates 2-5 can be ruled out early"

python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 5 --why "Candidates near periods 1.09d and 0.93d now dominate and are nearly tied; t=43.29 gives maximal predicted separation for that pair"

input.description: Check current state and remaining slots

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 7 --why "t=48.15 gives maximal separation for the P=1.08d vs P=2.5d pair while also stress-testing the remaining weaker alternatives"

content.text: Now pair (2,3) clearly dominates. Best slot is 13 (t=61.47) with max separation.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 13 --why "t=61.47 gives maximal separation for the leading P=1.08d candidate against its main remaining rival at P=13.2d"

python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 20 --why "Support flipped sharply after the last point, so confirming the P=13.2d vs P=1.08d pair at its best remaining separation t=70.27 before trusting the new leader"

python -m aliasbreaker.cli observe --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --slot 26 --why "Final budgeted point at t=78.56 targets the last non-negligible rival at P=0.93d to push the leading P=13.2d candidate past the resolution threshold"

content.text: Support for the P=13.21d candidate crossed theta (0.999986 ≥ 0.997). Finalizing with resolution.

input.command: python -m aliasbreaker.cli finalize --run runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1 --why "Support for the P=13.21d candidate rose to 0.99999 after confirmation points at t=70.27 and t=78.56 crossed theta, resolving the orbit and ruling out the initially favored short-period aliases"

content.text:
Campaign complete for **case-103** (run: `runs/dev-v1b-case-103-r1`).

**Result: Resolved** — candidate index 2, P = 13.21453 days, support = 0.999986 (θ = 0.997), using all 6 observations.

Summary of how it unfolded:
- Initial fit favored P≈1.24d and P≈5.24d roughly evenly (support ~0.28 each).
- First follow-up (t=35.3) flipped the picture entirely: those two collapsed and P≈1.09d/P≈0.93d became dominant and near-tied.
- Second point (t=43.3) pushed P≈1.09d to 0.87 support; a third (t=48.2) eliminated the P≈2.5d alternative and nudged P≈1.09d to 0.90.
- A high-separation point at t=61.5 caused a dramatic reversal — support swung to P≈13.21d (0.82), demoting the previously leading P≈1.09d candidate to 0.17.
- Given that reversal, spent a confirmation observation at t=70.27 (best separation for the 13.21d vs 1.09d pair), pushing support to 0.992 — just under threshold.
- Final observation at t=78.56 targeted the last non-negligible rival (P≈0.93d) and drove support to 0.999986, crossing θ.

This case illustrates exactly why the protocol calls for confirmation observations before trusting an early crossing — the true orbit here was not among the two candidates that looked dominant after the initial sparse data.
